Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. [G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.

The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.

- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).

Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).

- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).

- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-24.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.

items.content: TISSUE: Cells combine to perform same function.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes a group of cells a tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page identifies their working together to perform the same function as the defining feature.

teacher_understanding.question: Which words identify the functional basis of the definition?
teacher_understanding.answer: 'Perform same function' makes shared work, rather than mere closeness, central to the definition.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is grouping useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: A multicellular body needs coordinated tasks; specialised groups can perform particular jobs more effectively than isolated cells doing everything.

items.exam_note: Distinguish a tissue from an organ and from an arbitrary collection of cells.

unpack.consequence: The definition provides the starting level for tissue classification.
unpack.visual_verb: group cells into a working team
unpack.level_extra: A common function is more important than simply counting nearby cells.

items.content: When plant cells combine, they form plant tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue category is formed by plant cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Plant cells working together form plant tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this category differ from the next bullet's category?
teacher_understanding.answer: The distinction is the cells' origin: plant cells form plant tissues, whereas animal cells form animal tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: How should 'combine' be understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells become organised into cooperating groups; it does not mean their contents must fuse into one giant cell.

items.exam_note: Foundation for the plant-tissue classification below.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में मिलकर काम करने वाले cells के समूह
terms.everyday_image: पत्ते में साथ काम करते बहुत से छोटे हिस्से

why_chain.step: Plants need growth, support and transport.
Their cells form organised tissues for these jobs.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: tissues in a leaf or stem.
unpack.consequence: Plant tissues are classified in the lower chart.
unpack.visual_verb: zoom from leaf to grouped cells
unpack.level_extra: Do not apply animal-tissue names indiscriminately to plants.

items.content: When animal cells combine, they form animal tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which category comes from animal cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their organised groups constitute animal tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes this category from plant tissues here?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page separates the categories by whether the constituent cells belong to animals or plants.

teacher_understanding.question: Why do animals need organised groups of cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tasks such as movement, protection and communication require different specialised groups to cooperate.

items.exam_note: Keep plant and animal tissue classifications distinct.

terms.plain_meaning: जानवरों और हमारे शरीर में मिलकर काम करने वाले cells के समूह
terms.everyday_image: हाथ हिलाते समय साथ काम करती muscle

why_chain.step: An animal body must perform several different tasks.
Specialised cell groups share these tasks.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: muscle tissue in the human arm.
unpack.consequence: Introduces division of labour across tissues.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight cooperating groups in an arm
unpack.level_extra: Humans belong within the animal category.

items.content: Causes division of labour.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does tissue organisation lead to division of labour?
teacher_understanding.answer: Different groups can specialise in different jobs instead of each cell attempting the body's whole range of tasks.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this division operate in a body?
teacher_understanding.answer: For example, muscle cells contribute to movement while other specialised cells perform protection or communication.

items.exam_note: Conceptual reason for tissue specialisation.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग-अलग काम अलग टीमों में बाँटना
terms.everyday_image: घर में कोई खाना बनाता है, कोई सफाई करता है

why_chain.step: A body has more tasks than one kind of cell can efficiently perform.
Tissue organisation divides the work among specialised groups.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: movement and protection assigned to different tissues.
unpack.consequence: Explains reduced workload on individual cells.
unpack.visual_verb: distribute job cards among groups
unpack.level_extra: Division of labour means specialisation, not cell division.

items.content: Decreases workload on individual cells, hence leads to organisation.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the workload of an individual cell reduced?
teacher_understanding.answer: Specialisation means it need not perform every function required by the entire organism.

teacher_understanding.question: How does shared work produce organisation rather than disconnected groups?
teacher_understanding.answer: Specialised groups depend on one another and coordinate their activities within tissues, organs and organ systems.

teacher_understanding.question: What consequence does the page state?
teacher_understanding.answer: Reduced individual workload is linked to organisation.

items.exam_note: Understand specialisation and interdependence together.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग हिस्सों का तालमेल से पूरा काम चलाना
terms.everyday_image: अलग काम करती टीमें मिलकर अस्पताल चलाती हैं

why_chain.step: Many body functions must be managed together.
Sharing tasks reduces individual workload and supports organisation.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: digestive and transport functions cooperate after a meal.
unpack.consequence: Leads into the cell-to-organism hierarchy.
unpack.visual_verb: connect specialised teams
unpack.level_extra: Reduced workload does not mean cells cease their own essential life processes.

items.content: Cell → Tissues → Organ → Organ system → Organisms. Arrows connect successive levels of biological organisation, from component to larger organised whole.
items.type_note: The arrows represent levels of organisation rather than stages of a timed process.

teacher_understanding.question: What hierarchy is shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells are followed by tissues, organs, organ systems and organisms in increasing organisational scale.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the tissue level sit?
teacher_understanding.answer: It lies between the cell and the organ levels.

teacher_understanding.question: How are tissues and organs different?
teacher_understanding.answer: An organ brings different tissues together for a larger coordinated function; a tissue is a functional group of cells.

items.exam_note: Order-of-organisation and tissue-versus-organ questions.

terms.plain_meaning: एक बड़े काम के लिए साथ काम करने वाले organs
terms.everyday_image: खाना पचाने में साथ लगे पेट और आँत

why_chain.step: Complex body functions need cooperation beyond a single tissue.
Tissues form organs and organs cooperate in systems.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: muscle cell → muscle tissue → stomach → digestive system → human.
unpack.consequence: Prevents confusing a tissue with a whole organ.
unpack.visual_verb: nest smaller levels inside larger levels
unpack.level_extra: The hierarchy describes multicellular organisation; it is not universal to unicellular life.

items.content: Cell: starting level, pointing to Tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: What does Cell represent?
teacher_understanding.answer: A living structural and functional unit of an organism.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is it in the chain?
teacher_understanding.answer: It precedes Tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it contribute to the next level?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells cooperate in groups that perform shared functions.

items.exam_note: Smallest level shown.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर की छोटी जीवित इकाई
terms.everyday_image: इमारत की ईंट जैसा हिस्सा, पर खुद जीवित

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: a muscle cell.
unpack.consequence: Groups contribute to tissue formation.
unpack.visual_verb: zoom into one cell

items.content: Tissues: between Cell and Organ.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this level group?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells cooperating to perform a common function.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does this level occur in the hierarchy?
teacher_understanding.answer: After Cell and before Organ.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a tissue contribute to an organ?
teacher_understanding.answer: It supplies a particular function that combines with other tissues' functions.

items.exam_note: Do not equate one tissue with a whole organ.

terms.plain_meaning: एक काम में जुटे cells के समूह
terms.everyday_image: काम बाँटकर चलती एक टीम

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: muscle tissue in the stomach.
unpack.consequence: Tissues contribute to organs.
unpack.visual_verb: group cells

items.content: Organ: between Tissues and Organ system.

teacher_understanding.question: What is an organ?
teacher_understanding.answer: A body structure containing different tissues that cooperate in a particular function.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is Organ placed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Between Tissues and Organ system.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are multiple tissues useful within an organ?
teacher_understanding.answer: A task such as digestion needs movement, protection and other functions working together.

items.exam_note: Organ-versus-tissue distinction.

terms.plain_meaning: कई tissues से बना खास काम करने वाला शरीर का हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: पेट में कई हिस्से मिलकर खाना सँभालते हैं

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: stomach.
unpack.consequence: Organs cooperate within systems.
unpack.visual_verb: assemble tissues into an organ

items.content: Organ system: between Organ and Organisms.

teacher_understanding.question: What is an organ system?
teacher_understanding.answer: A set of organs cooperating in a major body function.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is it placed?
teacher_understanding.answer: After Organ and before Organisms.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it extend an organ's work?
teacher_understanding.answer: It coordinates several organs so different parts of a larger task can be completed.

items.exam_note: Correct hierarchy sequence.

terms.plain_meaning: एक बड़ा काम मिलकर करते organs
terms.everyday_image: खाना पचाने की जुड़ी हुई कार्य-श्रृंखला

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: digestive system.
unpack.consequence: Systems contribute to the whole organism.
unpack.visual_verb: link organs

items.content: Organisms: final level after Organ system.

teacher_understanding.question: What does Organisms refer to?
teacher_understanding.answer: Whole living individuals, rather than one of their component tissues or organs.

teacher_understanding.question: Where is the whole organism shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: At the end of the chain after Organ system.

teacher_understanding.question: How is the whole sustained?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its systems coordinate and depend on one another.

items.exam_note: Highest level in this particular diagram.

terms.plain_meaning: पूरे जीवित प्राणी या पौधे
terms.everyday_image: एक पूरा इंसान, सिर्फ उसका हाथ नहीं

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: a human or a flowering plant.
unpack.consequence: Completes the multicellular hierarchy.
unpack.visual_verb: zoom out to whole organism
unpack.level_extra: Not all organisms possess all the intermediate levels shown.

items.content: Comparison table with columns Mitosis and Meiosis and 11 numbered rows: occurrence, nuclear divisions, daughter-cell number, ploidy, frequency, products, phases, chromosome-number change, chromosome doubling, crossing over and type of division.
items.exam_note: Rows below preserve all comparisons, including questionable claims.

items.content: Mitosis: 1) It occurs in somatic cells. | Meiosis: 1) It occurs in germ cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which cell categories are contrasted?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table associates mitosis with somatic cells and meiosis with germ cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the difference between somatic and germ cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Somatic cells serve the body; the germ line contributes to sexual reproduction.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must this row not be treated as an absolute rule?
teacher_understanding.answer: Germ-line cells can also multiply by mitosis before meiosis. The row identifies usual roles, not exclusive permissions.

items.exam_note: Trap: germ-line cells can also undergo mitosis.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर के सामान्य काम करने वाले cells
terms.everyday_image: चोट के पास नई skin बनना

terms.plain_meaning: प्रजनन की cell-श्रृंखला से जुड़े cells
terms.everyday_image: अगली पीढ़ी तक जानकारी पहुँचाने की कड़ी

why_chain.step: Bodies need growth while sexual reproduction needs specialised reproductive cells.
Mitosis and meiosis meet these different needs.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside examples: dividing skin cells and meiotic cells in reproductive organs.
unpack.consequence: Connects division type with biological role.
unpack.visual_verb: split body-maintenance and reproduction pathways
unpack.level_extra: In plants, meiosis produces spores rather than directly producing gametes.

items.content: Mitosis: 2) Nucleus divides only once. | Meiosis: 2) Nucleus divides twice.

teacher_understanding.question: How many nuclear divisions does each have?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis has one; meiosis has two.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes the two meiotic divisions?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are two divisions useful in meiosis?
teacher_understanding.answer: They separate chromosome partners and then their copied strands, producing cells with a reduced chromosome-set number.

items.exam_note: One DNA replication before meiosis, not one before each division.

terms.plain_meaning: cell का हिस्सा जिसमें chromosome वाली जानकारी रहती है
terms.everyday_image: काम की निर्देश-पुस्तिका रखने की जगह

why_chain.step: Reproduction requires halving chromosome sets.
Meiosis uses two successive nuclear divisions.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: sperm formation.
unpack.consequence: Explains the next row's two-versus-four products.
unpack.visual_verb: divide once versus divide twice
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish nuclear division from DNA replication.

items.content: Mitosis: 3) Two daughter cells are formed. | Meiosis: 3) Four daughter cells are formed.

teacher_understanding.question: What product counts does the table give?
teacher_understanding.answer: Two daughter cells for mitosis and four for meiosis.

teacher_understanding.question: How do the branching patterns differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: One division yields two products; two successive divisions can yield four.

teacher_understanding.question: Does four products mean four functional gametes in every case?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. In human egg formation, unequal divisions produce one large ovum and smaller polar bodies.

items.exam_note: Do not equate four meiotic products with four functional eggs.

terms.plain_meaning: एक cell के बँटने से बने नए cells
terms.everyday_image: एक शाखा से निकलती नई शाखाएँ

why_chain.step: Copied material must be distributed into new cells.
One versus two divisions gives the usual two-versus-four product pattern.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: four products in sperm formation.
unpack.consequence: Product number must be read separately from chromosome number.
unpack.visual_verb: branch one into two and then four
unpack.level_extra: Standard numerical comparison; functional gamete count has exceptions.

items.content: Mitosis: 4) Daughter cells are diploid. | Meiosis: 4) Daughter cells are haploid.

teacher_understanding.question: Which ploidy does the book assign to the products?
teacher_understanding.answer: It assigns diploid products to mitosis and haploid products to meiosis.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the difference between diploid and haploid?
teacher_understanding.answer: Diploid means two chromosome sets, written 2n; haploid means one set, written n. Here n denotes one chromosome set, not a physical unit.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the mitosis claim qualified?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis preserves the starting ploidy; a haploid cell can also divide mitotically. Diploid products assume a diploid starting cell.

items.exam_note: Trap: mitosis does not necessarily create diploidy.

terms.plain_meaning: chromosomes के दो पूरे set
terms.everyday_image: निर्देशों की दो पूरी गड्डियाँ

terms.plain_meaning: chromosomes का एक पूरा set
terms.everyday_image: निर्देशों की एक पूरी गड्डी

why_chain.step: Fusion of reproductive cells would increase chromosome sets without reduction.
Meiosis supplies reduced-set products.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: human body cells usually have 46 chromosomes, gametes 23.
unpack.consequence: Links ploidy to chromosome conservation across generations.
unpack.visual_verb: show two sets becoming one set
unpack.level_extra: Ploidy counts sets, not DNA quantity.

items.content: Mitosis: 5) It occurs more frequently. | Meiosis: 5) It occurs less frequently.

teacher_understanding.question: What frequency contrast is printed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis is described as more frequent and meiosis as less frequent.

teacher_understanding.question: What difference in roles explains the broad comparison?
teacher_understanding.answer: Growth and replacement involve mitosis across many tissues; meiosis is restricted to particular reproductive stages and cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should this not be memorised as a fixed numerical law?
teacher_understanding.answer: Actual rates vary with tissue, organism, age and reproductive activity; the table gives no measured rate.

items.exam_note: Qualitative generalisation, not a universal rate.

terms.plain_meaning: तुलना में ज्यादा बार होना
terms.everyday_image: रोजमर्रा का काम बनाम खास मौके का काम

why_chain.step: Bodies repeatedly need growth and replacement.
Mitosis has a broader routine role than meiosis.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: continuing cell replacement in skin.
unpack.consequence: Reinforces maintenance-versus-reproduction roles.
unpack.visual_verb: contrast repeated repair with a reproductive pathway
unpack.level_extra: Avoid treating 'more frequent' as true for every individual tissue.

items.content: Mitosis: 6) Daughter cells form somatic organs. | Meiosis: 6) Daughter cells form gametes.

teacher_understanding.question: What destinations does the table assign to daughter cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Somatic organs for mitotic products and gametes for meiotic products.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these functions differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Somatic growth builds and maintains the body; gametes participate in fertilisation.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the meiosis wording need a plant-life-cycle qualification?
teacher_understanding.answer: In plants, meiosis generally forms spores; gametes develop later through the haploid phase and mitosis.

items.exam_note: Do not universally equate meiosis with direct gamete production.

terms.plain_meaning: fertilisation में मिलने वाले प्रजनन cells
terms.everyday_image: sperm और egg का मिलना

why_chain.step: Body maintenance and sexual reproduction have different chromosome needs.
Mitosis preserves sets while meiosis reduces them.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: human sperm and egg formation.
unpack.consequence: Links division to growth and reproduction.
unpack.visual_verb: route products toward body growth or reproduction
unpack.level_extra: Flag the plant spore-versus-gamete distinction.

items.content: Mitosis: 7) There is only one prophase, one metaphase one anaphase and one telophase. | Meiosis: 7) There are two of each phase and five sub-phases in prophase - 1.

teacher_understanding.question: How are the main phases counted?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table gives one occurrence of each named phase in mitosis and two in meiosis, with five subdivisions of prophase I.

teacher_understanding.question: What are the five subdivisions of prophase I?
teacher_understanding.answer: Leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is prophase I particularly elaborate?
teacher_understanding.answer: Homologous chromosomes pair and exchange genetic material, events not characteristic of ordinary mitotic prophase.

items.exam_note: Know prophase I as the pairing and crossing-over phase; avoid confusing it with prophase II.

terms.plain_meaning: meiosis के पहले division का शुरुआती चरण
terms.everyday_image: बँटवारे से पहले जोड़ीदार कागज़ मिलाकर तैयार करना

why_chain.step: Homologous partners must be prepared for separation.
Prophase I includes pairing and recombination before later separation.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: meiotic cells in reproductive organs.
unpack.consequence: Prepares the crossing-over comparison.
unpack.visual_verb: align phases in one versus two division cycles
unpack.level_extra: The five names explain the printed count; they are not printed individually on this page.

items.content: Mitosis: 8) Number of chromosomes are not changed in the daughter cells. | Meiosis: 8) Number of chromosomes are reduced to half.

teacher_understanding.question: How does chromosome number change?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is maintained in mitotic daughter cells and reduced to half through meiosis.

teacher_understanding.question: What symbolic comparison expresses this?
teacher_understanding.answer: For a diploid starting cell, mitosis gives 2n to 2n, while meiosis gives 2n to n; n means one chromosome set and has no measurement unit.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is halving important?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fusion of two haploid gametes restores the diploid number rather than doubling the species' chromosome number each generation.

items.exam_note: Core equational-versus-reduction distinction.

terms.plain_meaning: शुरुआत के मुकाबले chromosome संख्या आधी
terms.everyday_image: दो गड्डियों में से एक पूरी गड्डी मिलना

why_chain.step: Fertilisation joins chromosome sets from two gametes.
Meiotic reduction prevents repeated doubling across generations.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: 46 to 23 in human meiosis.
unpack.consequence: Explains reduction division.
unpack.visual_verb: count sets before and after division
unpack.level_extra: Compare final products with the starting cell, not DNA amount at an intermediate stage.

items.content: Mitosis: 9) Chromosome number doubles at the beginning of each cell division. | Meiosis: 9) Chromosome number is not doubled. It doubles after the end of first meiotic division.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the printed row claim?
teacher_understanding.answer: It claims chromosome-number doubling at the beginning of each mitotic division, and doubling after the first meiotic division.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the correct distinction between chromosome number and DNA replication?
teacher_understanding.answer: DNA replicates before mitosis and before meiosis I, producing sister chromatids without doubling the usual chromosome count. There is no DNA replication between meiosis I and II.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this printed row unsafe to learn literally?
teacher_understanding.answer: It confuses chromosome number with DNA amount and wrongly places doubling after meiosis I. Chromosomes are conventionally counted by centromeres, not by the number of DNA copies.

items.exam_note: Scientific error in source: teach the standard correction explicitly, not the printed claim as fact.

terms.plain_meaning: centromere के हिसाब से गिने गए chromosomes की संख्या
terms.everyday_image: किताब की नकल बनना और किताब के set बदलना अलग बातें हैं

why_chain.step: Daughter cells need copied genetic information.
DNA is copied before division, but meiosis has no second replication between its two divisions.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: a human cell still has 46 chromosomes after predivision DNA replication, although each has two sister chromatids.
unpack.consequence: Prevents a false inference about replication between meiotic divisions.
unpack.visual_verb: copy DNA while keeping chromosome and DNA counters separate
unpack.level_extra: This is a factual error, not merely a typographical spelling error.

items.content: Mitosis: 10) No crossing over in chromosomes. | Meiosis: 10) Crossing over occurs chromosomes [occurs in chromosomes].

teacher_understanding.question: What crossing-over contrast is printed?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table contrasts its absence in mitosis with its occurrence in meiosis.

teacher_understanding.question: What is crossing over?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is exchange of corresponding DNA segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during prophase I.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does it matter?
teacher_understanding.answer: It produces new combinations of genetic information, contributing to variation among meiotic products.

items.exam_note: Match crossing over with prophase I; the mitosis statement describes the standard comparison.

terms.plain_meaning: जोड़ीदार chromosomes की non-sister chromatids के बीच DNA के हिस्से बदलना
terms.everyday_image: मिलते-जुलते रंगीन फीते अपने हिस्से बदलें

why_chain.step: Sexual reproduction generates new combinations of inherited information.
Exchange between homologous partners contributes to these combinations.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: prophase I of meiosis.
unpack.consequence: Links meiosis with genetic variation.
unpack.visual_verb: exchange corresponding coloured segments
unpack.level_extra: Do not describe crossing over as exchange between unrelated chromosomes.

items.content: Mitosis: 11) Equation [Equational] division. | Meiosis: 11) Reduction division.

teacher_understanding.question: Which names summarise the two divisions?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table calls mitosis equational division and meiosis reduction division.

teacher_understanding.question: What do equational and reduction mean here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Equational preserves chromosome number in the products; reduction lowers the chromosome-set number.

teacher_understanding.question: Why distinguish meiosis I from meiosis II?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meiosis I is the reductional division; meiosis II separates sister chromatids and is equational with respect to chromosome sets.

items.exam_note: Trap: meiosis II is equational, despite meiosis being called reduction division overall.

terms.plain_meaning: chromosome set घटाने वाला division
terms.everyday_image: दो पूरे set से एक पूरा set होना

why_chain.step: Products must either preserve or reduce starting chromosome sets.
These outcomes give the terms equational and reductional.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: meiosis I reduces diploid to haploid.
unpack.consequence: Summarises the most important table distinction.
unpack.visual_verb: hold set count constant versus halve it
unpack.level_extra: Correct the printed word 'Equation' openly.

items.content: Table 7.3: Difference between mitosis in Plants and Animals. Columns: Plants | Animals. Four rows compare centrioles, asters, cell division and distribution.
items.exam_note: Plant-versus-animal mitosis comparison.

items.content: Plants: Centrioles are absent. | Animals: Centrioles are present.

teacher_understanding.question: What centriole contrast is shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: The plant column gives absence and the animal column presence.

teacher_understanding.question: Does absence of centrioles mean plant cells cannot form a spindle?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Typical higher-plant cells organise spindle microtubules without the animal-type centriole-containing centrosome.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the plant statement be qualified?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes typical higher-plant mitosis; centrioles occur in some plant groups or reproductive stages.

items.exam_note: Centriole absence does not imply spindle absence.

terms.plain_meaning: छोटी बेलन जैसी बनावटें जो animal cell के centrosome का हिस्सा होती हैं
terms.everyday_image: दो छोटी खोखली नलियाँ

why_chain.step: Chromosomes need an organised spindle for separation.
Plants and animals can organise this machinery differently.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: typical flowering-plant cells versus animal body cells.
unpack.consequence: Prepares the aster comparison.
unpack.visual_verb: contrast spindle poles with and without centrioles
unpack.level_extra: Avoid extending the textbook generalisation to every plant lineage.

items.content: Plants: Asters are not formed. | Animals: Asters are formed.

teacher_understanding.question: How are asters contrasted?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are absent in the plant column and formed in the animal column.

teacher_understanding.question: How is an aster different from the whole spindle?
teacher_understanding.answer: An aster is a star-like array of microtubules radiating near a spindle pole, not the entire chromosome-separating spindle.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the aster comparison accompany the centriole comparison?
teacher_understanding.answer: Typical animal centrosomes organise conspicuous radial arrays; higher-plant divisions usually lack this animal-type astral organisation.

items.exam_note: Aster-free does not mean spindle-free.

terms.plain_meaning: spindle के सिरों के पास तारे की तरह फैले धागों के समूह
terms.everyday_image: सूरज से बाहर निकलती किरणों का चित्र

why_chain.step: Dividing cells must position their division machinery.
Animal cells commonly use radial astral microtubule arrays.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: asters at poles of a typical animal mitotic cell.
unpack.consequence: Adds a visible distinction between the two division patterns.
unpack.visual_verb: radiate fibres from poles
unpack.level_extra: Recognise the star-like form without confusing it with chromosomes.

items.content: Plants: Cell division involves formation of a cell plate. | Animals: Cell division involves furrowing and cleavage of cytoplasm.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the cytoplasm divide in the two columns?
teacher_understanding.answer: Plants form a cell plate; animals divide by furrowing and cleavage.

teacher_understanding.question: What directional difference helps visualise this?
teacher_understanding.answer: The plant cell plate grows outward from the centre, whereas the animal cleavage furrow moves inward from the surface.

teacher_understanding.question: Why do plants use a cell plate?
teacher_understanding.answer: A rigid existing cell wall prevents the animal-style pinching mechanism; a new partition is assembled between daughter cells.

items.exam_note: Classic cell plate versus cleavage-furrow question.

terms.plain_meaning: दो नए plant cells के बीच बनने वाला नया बँटवारा
terms.everyday_image: एक कमरे के बीच नई दीवार बनाना

terms.plain_meaning: बाहर से अंदर की ओर खाँच पड़कर cell का बँटना
terms.everyday_image: नरम थैली को बीच से डोरी कसकर बाँटना

why_chain.step: Two daughter nuclei need separate cellular compartments.
A rigid plant wall favours building a partition, while animal cells can constrict.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: dividing root-tip cells versus animal cells.
unpack.consequence: Distinguishes cytokinesis from nuclear division.
unpack.visual_verb: build centre-out versus pinch outside-in
unpack.level_extra: The row primarily describes cytokinesis, not chromosome separation.

items.content: Plants: Occurs mainly at meristem. | Animals: Occurs in tissues throughout the body.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the table locate mitosis?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mainly at meristems in plants and in tissues throughout the animal body.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this say about growth distribution?
teacher_understanding.answer: Plant division is concentrated in growth regions, while animal cell replacement and growth occur in many distributed tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is 'throughout' not the same as 'every cell divides'?
teacher_understanding.answer: Many specialised animal cells divide little or not at all; the statement refers to tissue distribution, not universal cell activity.

items.exam_note: Retain 'mainly'; do not turn it into 'only'.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे की वह जगह जहाँ cells सक्रिय रूप से बँटकर बढ़त देते हैं
terms.everyday_image: जड़ या टहनी की बढ़ती नोक

why_chain.step: Plants need continuing growth at particular sites.
Meristems maintain dividing cells at these sites.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: root and shoot tips; animal skin renewal.
unpack.consequence: Directly introduces meristematic tissue in the chart.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight plant growth zones and distributed animal tissues
unpack.level_extra: Plant cells outside existing meristems can sometimes regain division capacity.

items.content: Classification of Plant Tissue. Root branches to Meristematic Tissue and Permanent Tissue. Meristematic Tissue branches to Apical Meristem, Lateral Meristem and Intercalary Meristem. Permanent Tissue branches to Simple and Complex. Simple branches to Paranchyma [Parenchyma], Collenchyma and Sclerenchyma. Sclerenchyma branches to Fibres and Sclereids. Complex branches to Xylem and Phloem. Visible Xylem entries: Tracheids; Vessels (Tracheae); Xylem parenchyma. Visible Phloem entries: Sieve tubes; Companion cells; Phloem parenchyma. The component lists meet the lower crop edge.
items.type_note: The visual is a branching classification, not merely a decorative figure.

teacher_understanding.question: Which are the two main plant-tissue branches?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meristematic Tissue and Permanent Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes the main branches?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meristematic tissues retain active division capacity; permanent tissues are differentiated for particular functions and generally no longer divide actively.

teacher_understanding.question: How should a student read the lower branches?
teacher_understanding.answer: Follow connecting lines rather than horizontal proximity: fibres and sclereids belong to sclerenchyma; xylem and phloem belong to complex permanent tissue.

items.exam_note: High-yield branch matching, odd-one-out and statement combinations.

terms.plain_meaning: एक आधार पर बड़े समूह को छोटे प्रकारों में बाँटना
terms.everyday_image: अलमारी में कपड़े अलग खानों में रखना

why_chain.step: Plant tissues perform different growth and maintenance tasks.
A branching hierarchy separates division capacity and cell-type composition.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside examples: growing root tip, supporting stem and transport in veins.
unpack.consequence: Provides the chapter's organising map.
unpack.visual_verb: unfold branches from the root
unpack.level_extra: Visible transport-component lists are not treated as complete because the image is cropped.

items.content: Classification of Plant Tissue: root label; branches to Meristematic Tissue and Permanent Tissue.
items.exam_note: Chart title and root; teaching is carried by i30 and the branch labels.

items.content: Meristematic Tissue: child of Classification of Plant Tissue; parent of Apical Meristem, Lateral Meristem and Intercalary Meristem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which three types occur under meristematic tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Apical, lateral and intercalary meristems.

teacher_understanding.question: How does meristematic tissue differ from permanent tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its cells actively divide to supply new cells rather than primarily performing mature specialised functions.

teacher_understanding.question: Why do plants retain these tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: They provide continuing sources of new cells for growth.

items.exam_note: Know all three position-based subdivisions.

terms.plain_meaning: नए cells बनाकर पौधे को बढ़ाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: पौधे की बढ़ती नोक की नई बनावट

why_chain.step: A plant needs new cells to grow.
Meristems preserve actively dividing cell populations.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: root tip.
unpack.consequence: Explains the three meristem positions.
unpack.visual_verb: multiply cells at growth zones
unpack.level_extra: Meristem types here are classified by position.

items.content: Apical Meristem: child of Meristematic Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which parent category contains apical meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meristematic Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does apical differ from lateral meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Apical meristems lie at root and shoot tips and increase length; lateral meristems chiefly increase thickness.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the tip extend?
teacher_understanding.answer: Division supplies new cells, which subsequently enlarge and differentiate.

items.exam_note: Match apical with tips and length growth.

terms.plain_meaning: जड़ और shoot की नोक पर नया बढ़ाव देने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: टहनी की आगे बढ़ती नोक

why_chain.step: Roots and shoots must extend into new space.
Tip meristems supply cells for length growth.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: a germinating seed's root tip.
unpack.consequence: Distinguishes length growth from girth growth.
unpack.visual_verb: extend a tip
unpack.level_extra: Apical means at the apex or tip.

items.content: Lateral Meristem: child of Meristematic Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which category contains lateral meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meristematic Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does its effect differ from apical growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lateral meristems increase girth in suitable stems and roots, rather than primarily extending tips.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is lateral growth useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: As a plant enlarges, additional conducting and supporting tissue can be supplied through secondary growth.

items.exam_note: Match lateral meristem or cambium with thickness.

terms.plain_meaning: किनारों के पास बढ़त देकर तना या जड़ मोटा करने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: पेड़ के तने का सालों में मोटा होना

why_chain.step: A larger plant needs greater support and transport capacity.
Lateral meristems add tissues that increase girth.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: vascular cambium in a woody stem.
unpack.consequence: Separates secondary growth from tip elongation.
unpack.visual_verb: thicken a stem cylinder
unpack.level_extra: Do not assume pronounced secondary growth in every plant.

items.content: Intercalary Meristem: child of Meristematic Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which category contains intercalary meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meristematic Tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How is its position different from an apical meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It occurs between mature regions, often near leaf or internode bases in grasses, rather than at the terminal tip.

teacher_understanding.question: How can it support regrowth after grazing?
teacher_understanding.answer: Basal growth regions may remain intact when upper portions are removed and can continue producing cells.

items.exam_note: Link grasses and regrowth with intercalary meristem.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे के पके हिस्सों के बीच बचा बढ़त वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: कटी घास का नीचे से फिर बढ़ना

why_chain.step: Grass may lose upper parts to cutting or grazing.
Retained basal growth zones allow continued growth.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: grass leaf bases.
unpack.consequence: Completes the positional meristem triad.
unpack.visual_verb: regrow grass from the base
unpack.level_extra: Intercalary means inserted between other regions.

items.content: Permanent Tissue: child of Classification of Plant Tissue; branches to Simple and Complex.

teacher_understanding.question: Which subdivisions are shown?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple and Complex permanent tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: How do permanent tissues differ from meristems?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are differentiated for particular functions and generally do not actively divide.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does differentiation matter?
teacher_understanding.answer: It equips cells for tasks such as storage, support and transport rather than continual cell production.

items.exam_note: Permanent does not mean dead.

terms.plain_meaning: खास काम के लिए विकसित tissue, जिसमें cells आम तौर पर सक्रिय रूप से नहीं बँटते
terms.everyday_image: प्रशिक्षण के बाद अपना तय काम सँभालती टीम

why_chain.step: New cells must perform the plant's everyday functions.
Differentiation produces specialised permanent tissues.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside examples: leaf storage tissue and stem transport tissue.
unpack.consequence: Sets up the simple-versus-complex distinction.
unpack.visual_verb: differentiate newly formed cells
unpack.level_extra: Some living permanent cells can regain division capacity.

items.content: Simple: child of Permanent Tissue; branches to Paranchyma [Parenchyma], Collenchyma and Sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissues are simple permanent tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes simple from complex tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: A simple tissue consists predominantly of one kind of similar cell; a complex tissue contains different cell types cooperating.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does 'simple' not mean unimportant?
teacher_understanding.answer: The term describes cell-type composition, not the importance or difficulty of its function.

items.exam_note: Xylem and phloem are not simple tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: मुख्य रूप से एक तरह के cells वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: एक जैसा काम जानने वाले लोगों की टीम

why_chain.step: Some functions can be performed by similar cells working together.
Such tissues are grouped as simple permanent tissues.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: parenchyma in potato storage tissue.
unpack.consequence: Organises the three named simple tissues.
unpack.visual_verb: group matching cell types
unpack.level_extra: Classification basis is composition, not number of cells.

items.content: Complex: child of Permanent Tissue; branches to Xylem and Phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which complex tissues are named?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem and phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How do complex tissues differ from simple tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Several cell types cooperate in a complex tissue, rather than predominantly one similar type.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can transport tissue need several types of cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Conduction, support, storage and metabolic assistance are complementary tasks.

items.exam_note: Match xylem and phloem to complex permanent tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग तरह के cells का मिलकर एक काम करना
terms.everyday_image: ड्राइवर, मैकेनिक और सहायक मिलकर परिवहन चलाएँ

why_chain.step: Plant transport needs more than a conducting channel alone.
Different cell types cooperate within xylem and phloem.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: vascular bundles in a stem.
unpack.consequence: Explains why multiple components are listed under each transport tissue.
unpack.visual_verb: assemble unlike cells into one transport team
unpack.level_extra: Complex tissue is still a tissue, not an organ.

items.content: Paranchyma [Parenchyma]: child of Simple permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which category contains parenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does typical parenchyma differ from sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parenchyma usually has living, relatively thin-walled cells; mature sclerenchyma commonly has thick lignified walls and dead cells.

teacher_understanding.question: How does its structure support storage?
teacher_understanding.answer: Living cells can accumulate materials such as starch and water within their contents.

items.exam_note: Preserve the printed spelling but teach Parenchyma.

terms.plain_meaning: आम तौर पर पतली दीवार वाले जीवित cells का tissue
terms.everyday_image: आलू के अंदर भोजन जमा रखने वाला हिस्सा

why_chain.step: Plants need places to store food and carry out metabolism.
Living parenchyma cells perform these adaptable roles.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: potato storage tissue.
unpack.consequence: Contrasts with the more specialised supporting simple tissues.
unpack.visual_verb: fill living cells with stored starch
unpack.level_extra: Xylem parenchyma and phloem parenchyma are components of complex tissues; names do not change their parent category.

items.content: Collenchyma: child of Simple permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Which category contains collenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it differ from typical parenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Collenchyma consists of living cells with unevenly thickened walls, commonly at the corners, providing flexible support.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is flexible support useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Young growing parts need strength while still being able to bend and elongate.

items.exam_note: Match living cells, uneven corner thickening and flexible support.

terms.plain_meaning: जीवित cells वाला tissue जो लचीला सहारा देता है
terms.everyday_image: नई डंडी का बिना टूटे थोड़ा मुड़ जाना

why_chain.step: Young plant parts need support without rigidly stopping growth.
Unevenly thickened living cells provide flexible reinforcement.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: young dicot stems and leaf stalks.
unpack.consequence: Separates flexible support from sclerenchyma's rigid support.
unpack.visual_verb: bend a supported young stalk
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse corner thickening with uniform lignified thickening.

items.content: Sclerenchyma: child of Simple permanent tissue; parent of Fibres and Sclereids.

teacher_understanding.question: Which forms branch from sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fibres and sclereids.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it differ from collenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sclerenchyma commonly has dead mature cells with thick lignified walls and gives rigid strength; collenchyma is living and more flexible.

teacher_understanding.question: Why do thick lignified walls provide strength?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their reinforced wall material resists deformation and helps support or protect plant parts.

items.exam_note: Fibres and sclereids are sclerenchyma forms, not separate main permanent-tissue branches.

terms.plain_meaning: मोटी मजबूत दीवारों वाला tissue जो कड़ा सहारा देता है
terms.everyday_image: नारियल का कठोर खोल

why_chain.step: Some plant parts need rigid support and protection.
Thick lignified walls provide mechanical strength.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: nut shells and supporting fibres.
unpack.consequence: Branches into two cell forms.
unpack.visual_verb: thicken and harden cell walls
unpack.level_extra: Remember the standard 'dead at maturity' qualification rather than assuming all permanent tissue is dead.

items.content: Fibres: child of Sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains fibres in this branch?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How do fibres differ from typical sclereids?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fibres are elongated and narrow; sclereids are generally shorter and can have varied shapes.

teacher_understanding.question: How does their shape support a plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: Long, thick-walled cells arranged together provide tensile reinforcement.

items.exam_note: Match elongated supporting cells to fibres.

terms.plain_meaning: लंबे पतले और मजबूत दीवार वाले सहारा देने वाले cells
terms.everyday_image: रस्सी के लंबे मजबूत रेशे

why_chain.step: Stems need resistance to pulling and bending.
Bundles of long fibres reinforce them.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: jute fibres.
unpack.consequence: Links tissue structure to useful plant fibres.
unpack.visual_verb: bundle elongated cells into a cable
unpack.level_extra: The chart's fibre branch is under sclerenchyma.

items.content: Sclereids: child of Sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which parent tissue contains sclereids?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How do sclereids differ from fibres?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are commonly shorter, variably shaped, thick-walled cells rather than long narrow fibres.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can they make plant material hard or gritty?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their strongly thickened walls form rigid cells that resist crushing.

items.exam_note: Connect stone cells with pear grittiness and hard shells.

terms.plain_meaning: छोटे या अलग आकार के बहुत कड़ी दीवार वाले cells
terms.everyday_image: नाशपाती खाते समय महसूस होने वाले किरकिराते कण

why_chain.step: Plant parts may need hard protection.
Rigid sclereids provide hardness and resistance.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: gritty cells in pear flesh.
unpack.consequence: Completes the two sclerenchyma forms.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight hard cells among softer cells
unpack.level_extra: Also called stone cells in standard descriptions.

items.content: Xylem: child of Complex permanent tissue; visible entries are Tracheids, Vessels (Tracheae), and Xylem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visible components belong to xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tracheids, vessels or tracheae, and xylem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How does xylem's main transport role differ from phloem's?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem mainly conducts water and minerals; phloem transports organic food materials.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is xylem classified as complex?
teacher_understanding.answer: Different cell types contribute to conduction, storage and support within one tissue.

items.exam_note: The visible list is cropped, not proof of an exhaustive component list.

terms.plain_meaning: पानी और minerals पहुँचाने वाला plant tissue
terms.everyday_image: जड़ों से पत्तों तक पानी की पाइपलाइन

why_chain.step: Leaves need water absorbed by roots.
Xylem provides conducting pathways with associated cells.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: wood and leaf veins.
unpack.consequence: Links complex composition with transport function.
unpack.visual_verb: carry water upward through a stem
unpack.level_extra: Not every xylem cell is dead; xylem parenchyma is living.

items.content: Tracheids: component listed under Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which complex tissue contains tracheids?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How do tracheids differ from vessel elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tracheids are elongated tapering cells without the open end perforations characteristic of vessel elements.

teacher_understanding.question: How can water move between tracheids?
teacher_understanding.answer: It passes through pits in adjoining walls; mature conducting tracheids lack living contents.

items.exam_note: Match tracheids to xylem, not phloem.

terms.plain_meaning: लंबे, नुकीले सिरों वाले पानी पहुँचाने के cells
terms.everyday_image: पास-पास लगी पतली नलियाँ जिनकी दीवारों से पानी आगे जाए

why_chain.step: Water needs a continuous route through plant tissues.
Overlapping tracheids pass water through wall pits.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: prominent water-conducting cells in conifer wood.
unpack.consequence: One conducting component of xylem.
unpack.visual_verb: pass water sideways through pits
unpack.level_extra: Tracheids and vessels are different conducting cell forms.

items.content: Vessels (Tracheae): component listed under Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains vessels or tracheae?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a vessel differ from a tracheid?
teacher_understanding.answer: Vessel elements join end to end through perforated end walls, forming a longer conducting tube.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this arrangement aid transport?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connected hollow elements provide a relatively continuous route for water flow.

items.exam_note: Plant tracheae here means vessels, not the human windpipe.

terms.plain_meaning: एक के ऊपर एक जुड़े cells से बनी पानी की लंबी नलियाँ
terms.everyday_image: पाइप के छोटे टुकड़ों को सिरों से जोड़ना

why_chain.step: Water must travel over long distances.
End-to-end vessel elements provide a continuous channel.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: vessels in flowering-plant xylem.
unpack.consequence: Another xylem conducting component.
unpack.visual_verb: join hollow elements end to end
unpack.level_extra: Mature conducting vessel elements are dead.

items.content: Xylem parenchyma: component listed under Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which complex tissue contains xylem parenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it differ from mature tracheids and vessel elements?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem parenchyma cells remain living and contribute storage and lateral transport rather than forming the main hollow conducting elements.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this component important for statements about xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It disproves the blanket claim that all xylem cells are dead.

items.exam_note: High-yield living component of xylem.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem में मौजूद जीवित cells जो सामान जमा करने और बगल की ओर पहुँचाने में मदद करें
terms.everyday_image: पानी की मुख्य लाइन के पास भंडार और सहायक रास्ते

why_chain.step: A transport tissue also needs local storage and exchange.
Living parenchyma provides these associated functions.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: living parenchyma within wood.
unpack.consequence: Shows why xylem is a mixed-cell complex tissue.
unpack.visual_verb: store material beside conducting tubes
unpack.level_extra: Do not classify the whole xylem as simple because it contains parenchyma.

items.content: Phloem: child of Complex permanent tissue; visible entries are Sieve tubes, Companion cells and Phloem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which phloem components are visible?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve tubes, companion cells and phloem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How does its transport role differ from xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem transports sugars and other organic materials from sources to sinks; xylem mainly carries water and minerals.

teacher_understanding.answer: Roots, growing parts and storage organs need materials made in photosynthetic tissues.

output.page_summary: Tissues are groups of cells performing a common function, enabling division of labour and organisation from cells to organisms. items.content: 10. Tissues and Its Types
items.exam_note: Chapter title.

items.content: TISSUE: Cells combine to perform same function.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes a group of cells a tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page identifies their working together to perform the same function as the defining feature.

teacher_understanding.question: Which words identify the functional basis of the definition?
teacher_understanding.answer: 'Perform same function' makes shared work, rather than mere closeness, central to the definition.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is grouping useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: A multicellular body needs coordinated tasks; specialised groups can perform particular jobs more effectively than isolated cells doing everything.

items.exam_note: Distinguish a tissue from an organ and from an arbitrary collection of cells.

terms.plain_meaning: एक जैसा काम मिलकर करने वाले cells का समूह
terms.everyday_image: एक काम सँभालती कर्मचारियों की टीम

why_chain.step: A large body needs many different jobs performed.
Cells group for a common function, forming tissues.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: muscle tissue in the arm helps produce movement.
unpack.consequence: The definition provides the starting level for tissue classification.
unpack.visual_verb: group cells into a working team
unpack.level_extra: A common function is more important than simply counting nearby cells.

items.content: When plant cells combine, they form plant tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue category is formed by plant cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Plant cells working together form plant tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this category differ from the next bullet's category?
teacher_understanding.answer: The distinction is the cells' origin: plant cells form plant tissues, whereas animal cells form animal tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: How should 'combine' be understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cells become organised into cooperating groups; it does not mean their contents must fuse into one giant cell.

items.exam_note: Foundation for the plant-tissue classification below.

why_chain.step: Plants need growth, support and transport.
Their cells form organised tissues for these jobs.

teacher_understanding.question: Which category comes from animal cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their organised groups constitute animal tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes this category from plant tissues here?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page separates the categories by whether the constituent cells belong to animals or plants.

teacher_understanding.question: Why do animals need organised groups of cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tasks such as movement, protection and communication require different specialised groups to cooperate.

items.exam_note: Keep plant and animal tissue classifications distinct.

items.content: Causes division of labour.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does tissue organisation lead to division of labour?
teacher_understanding.answer: Different groups can specialise in different jobs instead of each cell attempting the body's whole range of tasks.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this division operate in a body?
teacher_understanding.answer: For example, muscle cells contribute to movement while other specialised cells perform protection or communication.

items.exam_note: Conceptual reason for tissue specialisation.

items.content: Decreases workload on individual cells, hence leads to organisation.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the workload of an individual cell reduced?
teacher_understanding.answer: Specialisation means it need not perform every function required by the entire organism.

teacher_understanding.question: How does shared work produce organisation rather than disconnected groups?
teacher_understanding.answer: Specialised groups depend on one another and coordinate their activities within tissues, organs and organ systems.

teacher_understanding.question: What consequence does the page state?
teacher_understanding.answer: Reduced individual workload is linked to organisation.

items.exam_note: Understand specialisation and interdependence together.

teacher_understanding.answer: Cells are followed by tissues, organs, organ systems and organisms in increasing organisational scale.

teacher_understanding.question: Where does the tissue level sit?
teacher_understanding.answer: It lies between the cell and the organ levels.

teacher_understanding.question: How are tissues and organs different?
teacher_understanding.answer: An organ brings different tissues together for a larger coordinated function; a tissue is a functional group of cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which cell categories are contrasted?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table associates mitosis with somatic cells and meiosis with germ cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the difference between somatic and germ cells?
teacher_understanding.answer: Somatic cells serve the body; the germ line contributes to sexual reproduction.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must this row not be treated as an absolute rule?
teacher_understanding.answer: Germ-line cells can also multiply by mitosis before meiosis. The row identifies usual roles, not exclusive permissions.

why_chain.step: Bodies need growth while sexual reproduction needs specialised reproductive cells.
Mitosis and meiosis meet these different needs.

unpack.visual_verb: split body-maintenance and reproduction pathways

items.content: Mitosis: 2) Nucleus divides only once. | Meiosis: 2) Nucleus divides twice.

teacher_understanding.question: How many nuclear divisions does each have?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis has one; meiosis has two.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes the two meiotic divisions?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are two divisions useful in meiosis?
teacher_understanding.answer: They separate chromosome partners and then their copied strands, producing cells with a reduced chromosome-set number.

items.exam_note: One DNA replication before meiosis, not one before each division.

terms.plain_meaning: cell का हिस्सा जिसमें chromosome वाली जानकारी रहती है
terms.everyday_image: काम की निर्देश-पुस्तिका रखने की जगह

why_chain.step: Reproduction requires halving chromosome sets.
Meiosis uses two successive nuclear divisions.

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: sperm formation.
unpack.consequence: Explains the next row's two-versus-four products.
unpack.visual_verb: divide once versus divide twice
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish nuclear division from DNA replication.

items.content: Mitosis: 3) Two daughter cells are formed. | Meiosis: 3) Four daughter cells are formed.

teacher_understanding.question: What product counts does the table give?
teacher_understanding.answer: Two daughter cells for mitosis and four for meiosis.

teacher_understanding.question: How do the branching patterns differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: One division yields two products; two successive divisions can yield four.

teacher_understanding.question: Does four products mean four functional gametes in every case?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. In human egg formation, unequal divisions produce one large ovum and smaller polar bodies.

items.exam_note: Do not equate four meiotic products with four functional eggs.

terms.plain_meaning: एक cell के बँटने से बने नए cells
terms.everyday_image: एक शाखा से निकलती नई शाखाएँ

unpack.example_or_place: Outside example: four products in sperm formation.
unpack.consequence: Product number must be read separately from chromosome number.
unpack.visual_verb: branch one into two and then four

items.content: Mitosis: 4) Daughter cells are diploid. | Meiosis: 4) Daughter cells are haploid.

teacher_understanding.question: Which ploidy does the book assign to the products?
teacher_understanding.answer: It assigns diploid products to mitosis and haploid products to meiosis.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the difference between diploid and haploid?
teacher_understanding.answer: Diploid means two chromosome sets, written 2n; haploid means one set, written n. Here n denotes one chromosome set, not a physical unit.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the mitosis claim qualified?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mitosis preserves the starting ploidy; a haploid cell can also divide mitotically. Diploid products assume a diploid starting cell.

items.exam_note: Trap: mitosis does not necessarily create diploidy.

unpack.consequence: Links ploidy to chromosome conservation across generations.
